en: to be wiped; to be cleaned

examples.ko: 아침에 보니 창문이 깨끗하게 닦여 있어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw that the windows had been wiped clean.

examples.ko: 이 얼룩은 아무리 문질러도 안 닦여요.
examples.en: This stain won't come off no matter how much I rub it.
After mopping, the floor was wiped clean and shiny.

examples.ko: 이 천은 먼지가 잘 닦이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: This cloth seems to wipe dust off well.

examples.ko: 아직 닦이지 않은 접시가 하나 남았어요.
examples.en: There is one plate left that hasn't been wiped yet.

examples.ko: 말끔히 닦인 신발을 보니 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel good seeing the shoes wiped spotless.

explain: '닦다'의 피동이라서 닦는 사람보다 닦이는 물건과 그 상태를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '닦아지다'도 써요. 사람이 닦았다고 말할 때는 '닦아 놨어요'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The classroom floor has been wiped clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 닦은 결과의 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state after something has been wiped.

phrases.en: Glass gets wiped clean easily with this cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 쉽게 깨끗해진다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something gets clean easily.

phrases.en: The stain doesn't wipe off easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '닦이다'와 비슷한 뜻으로, 주로 안 지워질 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 닦이다; often used when something won't come off.

explain_en: This is the passive of '닦다' and focuses on the thing being wiped and its state rather than the person. '닦아지다' is used with a similar meaning. When saying a person wiped something, '닦아 놨어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Please write your name on the top of the box.
The top of the desk has turned white with dust.
The top of the cake is covered in cream.

examples.ko: 윗면을 위로 해서 놓아야 깨지지 않아요.
examples.en: Put it with the top side facing up so it doesn't break.
The color of the top side is different from the bottom.
The wrapping paper on top has torn.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫면'이에요. 상자, 책상, 케이크처럼 모양이 있는 물건의 위쪽 면을 말할 때 써요. 방향만 말할 때는 그냥 '위쪽'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put strawberries on the top part of the cake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '면'이 아니라 위쪽 부분 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the whole upper part, not just the surface.

phrases.en: There is a hole on the upper side of the box.
phrases.nuance_ko: '윗면'을 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out way of saying 윗면.

phrases.en: The top and bottom surfaces are different colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위아래 면을 함께 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing the top and bottom surfaces.

explain_en: The opposite is '아랫면' (bottom side). It is used for the top surface of an object with a shape, such as a box, desk or cake. If you only mean direction, you simply say '위쪽'.

examples.en: The windowpane is broken, so wind comes in.
A ball flew over and nearly broke the windowpane.
In winter, steam fogs up the windowpane.
I brought a rag to clean the windowpanes.
This house is quiet because the windowpanes are thick.
I can hear raindrops hitting the windowpane.

explain: 창문에 끼워진 유리 그 자체를 가리켜요. 창문 전체를 말할 때는 '유리창'이라고도 하는데, 깨지거나 닦거나 두께를 말할 때는 '창유리'가 잘 맞아요. '창유리가 깨지다', '창유리를 닦다'처럼 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I wiped the windowpanes clean on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유리 부분을 청소할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for cleaning the glass part.

phrases.example: 창유리가 두꺼워서 소리가 잘 안 들려요.
phrases.en: The windowpane is thick, so I can't hear sound well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유리의 두께를 말할 때 '창유리'가 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: 창유리 fits well when talking about glass thickness.

phrases.en: I opened the window and enjoyed the breeze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창문 전체를 말할 때는 '유리창'이라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When talking about the whole window, 유리창 is also used.

explain_en: It points to the glass itself that is set in a window. For the whole window you can also say '유리창', but '창유리' fits when talking about breaking, cleaning or thickness. It goes with phrases like '창유리가 깨지다' and '창유리를 닦다'.

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the sewer got blocked.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 하수도 공사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood is having sewer work done.
A smell was coming up from the sewer, so I reported it.

examples.ko: 시청에서 낡은 하수도를 새로 바꾸기로 했어요.
examples.en: The city hall decided to replace the old sewer.
Water that flows into the sewer goes to a treatment plant.

examples.ko: 하수도는 우리 눈에 잘 안 보이지만 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: Sewers are hard to see, but they are absolutely necessary.

explain: 쓰고 난 더러운 물이 흘러가는 길이에요. 깨끗한 물이 들어오는 '상수도'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: When it rains, there is a smell from the sewer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하수도에서 나는 안 좋은 냄새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the bad smell coming from the sewer.

phrases.en: The city hall is repairing the sewer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고치다'와 함께 수리하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 고치다 to talk about repair work.

phrases.en: Water supply and sewerage are essential for a city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝말인 '상수도'와 함께 묶어서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with its counterpart 상수도.

explain_en: It is the system that carries away used, dirty water. It is easy to remember as a pair with '상수도', which brings in clean water.

examples.en: I arrived home, opened the front door, and went in.

examples.ko: 현관문 앞에 택배 상자가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A delivery box is sitting in front of the front door.
I always lock the front door when I go out.
The front door slammed shut in the wind.
For security, I changed the front door password.
I hear someone knocking on the front door.

explain: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗고 들어가요. 그래서 문 안쪽의 신발 벗는 공간을 '현관'이라고 따로 불러요. 요즘은 열쇠 대신 '도어락' 번호로 여는 집이 많아요.

phrases.en: When you come in, please be sure to close the front door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열고 닫을 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요. 반대는 '현관문을 열다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic verb pairing for opening and closing the door; the opposite is 현관문을 열다.

phrases.en: I always lock the front door when I go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 나갈 때 문을 잠근다는 뜻이에요. '문을 닫다'보다 열쇠나 도어락으로 잠그는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to lock the door when leaving; it stresses locking with a key or door lock, more than just closing.

phrases.en: Please wait a moment in front of the front door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 문 바로 앞 장소를 말할 때 써요. 택배나 손님 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the spot right in front of the door; common when talking about deliveries or guests.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the front door

explain_en: In a Korean home you take off your shoes at the entrance. That is why the shoe-removing space just inside the door has its own name, '현관'. These days many homes open with a '도어락' (digital door lock) code instead of a key.

t90.ax: The front door slammed shut in the wind.

examples.en: A long hose is lying in the garden.

examples.ko: 호스는 쓰고 나서 잘 감아 두세요.
examples.en: Please coil the hose neatly after using it.
Dad holds a hose and washes the car.
There is a hole in the hose, so water leaks.
I watered the flowerpots with a hose.
I pressed the end of the hose with my hand.

explain: '소방 호스', '고무 호스'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여 써요. 딱딱한 금속이나 플라스틱 관은 '파이프'라고 해서 부드러운 '호스'와 구분해요.

phrases.en: The rubber hose was old, so I bought a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 앞에 붙여 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the material first tells the type.

phrases.en: They put out the fire with a fire hose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 끄는 데 쓰는 호스예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A hose used to put out fires.

phrases.en: Every morning I water the flowers with a hose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호스를 도구로 쓰는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the hose is the tool for the job.

explain_en: A type goes in front, as in '소방 호스' and '고무 호스'. Rigid metal or plastic tubes are called '파이프', which separates them from a flexible '호스'.

examples.en: The moon is hidden behind the clouds, so I can't see it.

examples.ko: 앞사람 키가 커서 화면이 반쯤 가려졌어요.
examples.en: The person in front is tall, so half the screen is blocked.

examples.ko: 나무에 가려져서 간판이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The sign is hidden by the trees and is hard to see.

examples.ko: 가방을 이불로 덮었지만 다 가려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: I covered the bag with a blanket, but it wasn't completely hidden.

examples.ko: 이 커튼을 치면 창문이 완전히 가려질까요?
examples.en: If I close this curtain, will the window be fully covered?

examples.ko: 큰 건물에 가려져서 바다가 안 보여요.
examples.en: The sea is hidden by the big building, so I can't see it.

explain: '가리다'의 피동으로, 무엇이 앞을 막아서 안 보이게 되었다는 느낌이에요. 단순히 '안 보이다'보다 막고 있는 것이 있다는 점이 달라요. '승부가 가려지다'처럼 결과가 분명하게 정해질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 모자에 가려진 얼굴이 잘 안 보여요.
phrases.en: I can't see the face hidden by the hat well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가려지다'를 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 말(-ㄴ)로 바꿔서, 무엇에 막혀 안 보이는 대상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of the verb, used to describe a thing that is blocked from view.

phrases.en: The sun was hidden by the clouds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 가려진 상황을 해요체 과거형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense in polite speech, used to say that something has already become blocked from view.

phrases.example: 커튼을 쳐도 창문이 다 가려지지 않아요.
phrases.en: Even with the curtain closed, the window isn't fully covered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완전히 막히지 않고 조금 보일 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, used when something is not fully blocked and can still be seen.

explain_en: It is the passive of '가리다', and it feels like something is standing in front and blocking the view. Compared with plain '안 보이다', it points to something that is blocking. It is also used when a result gets clearly decided, as in '승부가 가려지다'.

en: to be paid; to be settled

examples.en: Please check whether it can be paid by card.
The ordered item is paid for automatically.

examples.ko: 실수로 같은 물건이 두 번 결제됐어요.
examples.en: The same item was charged twice by mistake.
A text arrives once it is paid, so please check.

examples.ko: 아직 결제되지 않아서 상품을 보낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been paid yet, so we can't send the goods.

examples.ko: 결제된 금액은 다음 달에 카드값에서 빠져요.
examples.en: The amount that was paid comes out of the card bill next month.

explain: '결제하다'는 사람이 돈을 내는 일이고, '결제되다'는 결제가 처리된 상태를 말해요. 앱, 인터넷 쇼핑, 카드 문자에서 자주 나와요. 가게에서 직접 낼 때는 '계산하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The card payment doesn't go through in the app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결제가 처리되지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 앱이나 인터넷 쇼핑 문제를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a payment does not get processed. It is common for app and online shopping problems.

phrases.en: Check your text message to see if the order payment went through.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는지'는 결과를 모를 때 확인하는 말이에요. 카드 문자와 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-neunji' is used when you check an unknown result. It often goes with card text messages.

phrases.en: It was charged twice by mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 돈이 두 번 나갔다는 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to report a problem where the same payment was charged twice.

explain_en: 결제하다 is a person paying, while 결제되다 states that the payment has been processed. It shows up in apps, online shopping and card text messages. At a shop counter, 계산하다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: payment processed, esp. by card or transaction
gh: given out by the payer: wages, benefits
money handed over for goods or services
paid to an authority: taxes, fees, bills

p.n: 결제 stresses the transaction going through; 지불 just says the money was paid.

t90.ax: The ordered item is paid for automatically.

examples.en: The road curves to the right.
The wire bent easily.
If your back is bent, it can hurt.
It's an old nail, so it bends easily.

examples.ko: 구부러진 길을 따라 걸으면 바다가 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk along the curved road, you reach the sea.
As she grew older, my grandmother's back became bent.

explain: 물건이나 길이 저절로 휘어 있는 상태를 말해요. 사람이 일부러 구부릴 때는 '구부리다'를 써서 '무릎을 구부리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Please walk along the curved road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 모양을 설명하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used before a noun to describe its shape.

phrases.en: This stick doesn't bend easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단해서 휘지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is stiff and does not bend.

phrases.en: The branch bent in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이고, 힘을 받아 둥글게 되는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, with a stronger sense of curving under force.

explain_en: It describes a thing or road that is bent on its own. When a person bends something on purpose, use '구부리다', as in '무릎을 구부리다' (bend one's knees).

examples.en: The tree roots stretch deep into the ground.
A tree root was sticking out of the road and I almost tripped.
Many trees were pulled out by the roots in the typhoon.
Please give plenty of water around the tree's roots.

examples.ko: 이 나무뿌리는 말려서 차로 끓여 마셔요.
examples.en: You dry this tree root and boil it as tea.
The paving stones are lifted up because of the tree roots.

explain: 그냥 '뿌리'라고 해도 돼요. 나무인 것을 분명히 하고 싶을 때 '나무뿌리'라고 말해요. '뿌리'는 '문제의 뿌리'처럼 근본을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: This plant has long roots.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나무뿌리'보다 짧고 식물 전체에 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 나무뿌리 and works for any plant.

phrases.en: I tripped on a tree root on the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에 튀어나온 뿌리에 발이 걸릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when your foot catches on a root sticking out.
phrases.en_equiv: to trip on a tree root

phrases.example: 이 나무는 나무뿌리가 깊어서 잘 쓰러지지 않아요.
phrases.en: This tree has deep roots, so it doesn't fall over easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뿌리의 길이를 말할 때 형용사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with an adjective to describe how deep roots are.

explain_en: You can simply say '뿌리'. People say '나무뿌리' when they want to make clear it is a tree's root. '뿌리' is also used figuratively for the origin of something, as in '문제의 뿌리'.

t90.ax: You dry this tree root and boil it as tea.

examples.en: I watched a baseball game in a dome.

examples.ko: 돔 안에서는 비가 와도 경기를 해요.
examples.en: Inside the dome, games go on even when it rains.
This city's dome is also used as a concert hall.

examples.ko: 돔의 지붕이 열리는 모습을 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the dome's roof open for the first time.
In autumn, I go to the dome to see concerts.
When the dome is closed, sound echoes loudly.

explain: 영어 dome에서 온 외래어예요. 한국에서는 '고척스카이돔'처럼 지붕이 있는 경기장 이름에 나와요. 지붕이 있는 야구장을 '돔구장'이라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: I go to the dome stadium on weekends to watch baseball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지붕이 있는 야구장을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a baseball stadium with a roof.

phrases.en: It's cool inside the dome even in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안'을 붙여 지붕 아래 안쪽 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '안' refers to the space inside the dome.

phrases.en: This concert is held at the dome.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 경기나 행사가 돔에서 한다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에서', it says a game or event takes place at the dome.
phrases.en_equiv: to be held at the dome

explain_en: It is a loanword from the English 'dome'. In Korea it appears in the names of roofed stadiums such as '고척스카이돔'. A baseball park with a roof is also called '돔구장'.
